The University of Freiburg in 1961

After [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the University of Freiburg was reopened. New buildings for natural sciences were erected in the *Institutsviertel* ("institute quarter").
In the postwar years, the ideas of ordoliberalism, developed earlier by economists of the Freiburg School, such as [Walter Eucken](/wiki/Walter_Eucken "Walter Eucken"), [Franz Böhm](/wiki/Franz_B%C3%B6hm "Franz Böhm"), Hans Grossmann-Doerth, and Leonhard Miksch, drove the creation of the German [social market economy](/wiki/Social_market_economy "Social market economy") and its attendant *[Wirtschaftswunder](/wiki/Wirtschaftswunder "Wirtschaftswunder")*. Nobel Prize winner and former professor at the University of Freiburg, [Friedrich Hayek](/wiki/Friedrich_Hayek "Friedrich Hayek"), is also associated with this theory. He directed the [Walter Eucken Institut](/wiki/Walter_Eucken_Institut "Walter Eucken Institut"), an economic [think tank](/wiki/Think_tank "Think tank") in Freiburg cooperating with the university. Arnold Bergstraesser, considered a founding father or German political science after World War II, was also a professor at the University of Freiburg. His research group later formed what is now the Arnold Bergstraesser Institute for sociocultural research at the university.

Main article: [Knicks–Celtics rivalry](/wiki/Knicks%E2%80%93Celtics_rivalry "Knicks–Celtics rivalry")

The New York Knicks and the [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") are two of the three remaining teams from the original 1946 NBA (the other is the [Golden State Warriors](/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors")). The rivalry stems from the old rivalry between the cities of New York City and [Boston](/wiki/Boston "Boston"), which is also mirrored in both the [Yankees–Red Sox](/wiki/Yankees%E2%80%93Red_Sox_rivalry "Yankees–Red Sox rivalry") and [Jets–Patriots](/wiki/Jets%E2%80%93Patriots_rivalry "Jets–Patriots rivalry") rivalries. The fact that Boston and New York City are only 190 miles apart contributes to it.

The teams have met nine times in the postseason. The last time was in the [2012–13 season](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_NBA_season "2012–13 NBA season"), when [Carmelo Anthony](/wiki/Carmelo_Anthony "Carmelo Anthony") won the 2013 scoring title and helped them win the Atlantic Division for the first time since 1994. The Knicks faced the Celtics, who were without [Rajon Rondo](/wiki/Rajon_Rondo "Rajon Rondo") because of a mid-season injury, in the 1st round of the [2013 playoffs](/wiki/2013_NBA_playoffs "2013 NBA playoffs"). In both games 1 and 2, Celtics had a lead going into halftime but were held to 25 and 23 points respectively in the second half, which was an all-time low for the franchise in the playoffs. Knicks gained a 3–0 lead in the series, but Boston avoided elimination in games 4 and 5. In game six, Knicks once led by 26 points in the fourth quarter, then the Celtics went onto a 20–0 run in less than 5 minutes to make it a close game, but Knicks still won and moved on to round 2.

In [late antiquity](/wiki/Late_antiquity "Late antiquity"), Gaul was divided into Germanic kingdoms and a remaining Gallo-Roman territory. [Celtic Britons](/wiki/Celtic_Britons "Celtic Britons"), fleeing the [Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain](/wiki/Anglo-Saxon_settlement_of_Britain "Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain"), settled in west [Armorica](/wiki/Armorica "Armorica"); the Armorican peninsula was renamed [Brittany](/wiki/Brittany "Brittany"), and [Celtic culture](/wiki/Celts "Celts") was revived.

The first leader to unite all Franks was [Clovis I](/wiki/Clovis_I "Clovis I"), who began his reign as king of the [Salian Franks](/wiki/Salian_Franks "Salian Franks") in 481, routing the last forces of the Roman governors in 486. Clovis said he would be baptised a Christian in the event of victory against the [Visigothic Kingdom](/wiki/Visigothic_Kingdom "Visigothic Kingdom"), which was said to have guaranteed the battle. Clovis [regained the southwest from the Visigoths](/wiki/Franco-Visigothic_Wars "Franco-Visigothic Wars") and was baptised in 508. Clovis was the first [Germanic](/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples") conqueror after the [Fall of the Western Roman Empire](/wiki/Fall_of_the_Western_Roman_Empire "Fall of the Western Roman Empire") to convert to Catholic Christianity; thus France was given the title "Eldest daughter of the Church" by the papacy,[[32]](#cite_note-42) and French kings were called "the Most Christian Kings of France".
